description.text: Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc. ("HII", the "Company", "we", "us", or "our") is a global, all-domain defense partner, building and delivering the world's most powerful, survivable naval ships and technologies that safeguard America’s seas, sky, land, space, and cyber. For more than a century, our Ingalls Shipbuilding segment ("Ingalls") in Mississippi and Newport News Shipbuilding segment ("Newport News") in Virginia have built more ships in more ship classes than any other U.S. naval shipbuilder, making us America's largest shipbuilder. Our Mission Technologies segment develops integrated technology solutions and products that enable today's connected, all-domain force. Headquartered in Newport News, Virginia, we employ over 44,000 people domestically and internationally. We conduct most of our business with the U.S. Government, primarily the Department of War (the "Department"). As prime contractor, principal subcontractor, team member, or partner, we participate in many high-priority U.S. defense programs. Ingalls includes our non-nuclear ship design, construction, repair, and maintenance businesses. Newport News includes all of our nuclear ship design, construction, overhaul, refueling, and repair and maintenance businesses.

about.description_short: HII is America's largest shipbuilder, delivering the world's most powerful ships and all-domain mission technologies, including unmanned systems, to U.S. and allied defense customers. HII is the largest producer of unmanned underwater vehicles for the U.S. Navy and the world. With a more than 140-year history of advancing U.S. national security, HII builds and integrates defense capabilities extending from the core fleet to C6ISR, AI/ML, EW and synthetic training. Headquartered in Virginia, HII's workforce is 45,000 strong.

analysis_md:
# HII — Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc.
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-19. Market cap $10.611B at $270.00 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, ttm.json, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
America's largest military shipbuilder: Newport News (sole U.S. designer/builder/refueler of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, one of only two builders of nuclear submarines, co-building Virginia- and Columbia-class with General Dynamics), Ingalls (amphibious assault ships, surface combatants, Coast Guard cutters), and Mission Technologies (unmanned systems, AI/cyber/C5ISR). Revenue FY2025 $12.484B, up 8.2% YoY. Backlog $57.3B at 2026-06-30 (search: Q2 2026 reports), with $6.7B of Q2 awards and a $5.1B sole-source Truman refueling/complex overhaul award in September 2026. Q2 2026 revenue $3.418B, up 10.9% YoY, EPS $5.27; management raised 2026 shipbuilding revenue guidance to $10.2–$10.4B and shipbuilding margin guidance to 6.0–6.5%.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,196,000,000; capex $402,000,000; SBC $54,000,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $740,000,000 = $18.83/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share in dcf_numbers.json)
- Maintenance version FY2025: $379,000,000 as printed in financials_history.csv — quoted only with a defect attached: the engine's `delta_nwc` does not exclude current debt, so the disappearance of the $503M FY2024 current maturity (total debt $3,203M → $2,700M in FY2025 — a financing event, not an operating outflow) enters as a +$226M working-capital increase. Excluding current debt from NWC on the statements.json balance sheet (NWC −$91M in FY2024 → −$368M in FY2025, a $277M decrease), the maintenance figure recomputes to ≈$882,000,000 (NI $605M + D&A $329M − min(capex, D&A) $329M − ΔNWC −$277M) — above, not below, the conservative figure. The headline conservative OE ($740M) does not use `delta_nwc` and is unaffected. The residual difference between the two definitions is the working-capital / retiree-benefit timing that swings this business year to year (see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE and OE_VOLATILE below).
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but the per-share series is violently lumpy: FY2021 $9.83, FY2022 $11.12, FY2023 $16.14, FY2024 $0.08, FY2025 $18.83 (financials_history.csv). FY2024 OCF collapsed to $393M; FY2025 rebounded to $1,196M.
- Net debt $1,926,000,000 (dcf_numbers.json), plus lease liabilities $281,000,000 in the CSV latest row — see CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED / HIGH_NET_DEBT below. No buybacks in FY2025 (per the FY2025 earnings call summary found in research); dividends paid $213M in FY2025 per the same source, $216M TTM in fundamentals.json.

**Base used = median of the last 3 fiscal years' OE/share: $16.14/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the three years are FY2023 $16.14, FY2024 $0.08, FY2025 $18.83, so the median is the FY2023 figure). The latest-FY figure ($18.83) is rejected as the base because FY2025 OCF was flattered by a $170M trade-working-capital decrease and a $203M deferred-tax swing (10-K cash-flow table, see NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE); the median is the conservative, cycle-smoothing choice the engine is designed to make here.

**TTM rejected — with the legs quoted (ttm.json, through 2026-06-30):**
- OCF: FY $1,196,000,000 − prior-YTD $428,000,000 + current-YTD −$421,000,000 = **TTM $347,000,000**
- Capex: FY $402,000,000 − prior-YTD $163,000,000 + current-YTD $193,000,000 = **TTM $432,000,000**
- SBC: FY $54,000,000 − prior-YTD $33,000,000 + current-YTD $31,000,000 = **TTM $52,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **39,400,000**
- **TTM OE total −$137,000,000 → TTM OE/share −$3.48**
- The TTM figure is a working-capital timing artifact, not a run-rate: H1 2026 OCF was −$421M (Q1 alone −$390M on a $640M trade-working-capital increase, per the Q1 2026 10-Q summary found in research; Q2 OCF −$31M), while management reiterated full-year 2026 free-cash-flow guidance of $500–$600M at Q2, which requires essentially all of it in H2. This is the same lumpiness that printed FY2024 OE/share at $0.08 and FY2025 at $18.83. Using the TTM base would score a timing trough as a permanent loss; the 3-year median base is used instead, and the TTM collapse is instead reflected in the widened bear weight below. Basis note: fundamentals.json's own TTM block prints capex of $429,000,000 and TTM OE of −$134,000,000 for the same window — a $3M leg difference from ttm.json's $432,000,000 / −$137,000,000, because the two generators build the prior-YTD leg from different filing generations. ttm.json is the TTM of record for this run; the $3M touches neither the rejection nor the scored median base.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate-strong franchise, capped economics
Justification: an irreplaceable sole-source position in nuclear carriers and a duopoly in nuclear submarines, with a $57.3B backlog — but the customer is a monopsonist that caps margins by contract structure, and measured returns have compressed to single digits.
- FOR: Sole U.S. designer, builder and refueler of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers (Newport News) — the Truman RCOH award was made without competition because only Newport News has the facilities and knowledge; one of only two nuclear-submarine builders; barriers are effectively absolute (nuclear certification, dry docks, cleared skilled workforce, decades of Navy integration); $57.3B backlog at 2026-06-30 gives multi-year revenue visibility; every carrier built creates a ~50-year refueling/overhaul tail at the same sole-source yard.
- AGAINST: Single-customer concentration — substantially all backlog is U.S. government orders; the government sets the economics: cost-plus and fixed-price-incentive contracts cap upside and leave cost overruns, labor shortages and throughput delays with HII; no pricing power in the commercial sense; Mission Technologies competes in contested services markets; measured profitability has structurally compressed (below).
- **ROIC / margin evidence (fundamentals.json `roic_proxy` series):** ROIC proxy was 29.0% / 23.4% / 32.0% / 21.1% / 22.3% in FY2016–FY2020, then fell to 8.2% (FY2021), 7.7% (FY2022), 10.2% (FY2023), 6.5% (FY2024), 7.3% (FY2025). Operating margin compressed in parallel from 12.4% (FY2016) to 5.4% / 5.3% / 6.8% / 4.6% / 5.3% in FY2021–FY2025. Gross margin is only captured in fundamentals.json for FY2016 (38.0%) and FY2017 (40.3%); the later years' COGS tag is not separated there, so the operating-margin series is the usable trend. A moat of 7+ is not justified: recent ROIC sits in single digits, not well above the cost of capital through the recent cycle — the franchise is durable but its economics are contract-capped. Hence 6.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine's blended base start is 7.3% (components: revenue CAGR 5y 5.93%, 3y 5.35%, latest revenue YoY +8.23%, OE/share CAGR 2y 8.00%). Against actual prints — FY2025 revenue +8.2%, Q2 2026 revenue +10.9% YoY, raised 2026 shipbuilding revenue guidance — the 7.3% base start sits *below* the latest revenue print, which is appropriate here because OE, not revenue, is being grown, and OE conversion is the weak link (H1 2026 OCF negative; full-year FCF guided below FY2025's level). The super-bull start (19.3%) is above any recent print and is therefore held to a 10% probability: it requires both throughput growth and a margin recovery toward the pre-2021 operating-margin range. Probabilities were shifted bear-ward from the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults to **15/30/30/15/10** per the OE_VOLATILE resolution (45% on bear-or-worse); offsets and OE multipliers are the defaults (−12/−5/0/+5/+12pp; 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25). Price $270.00.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | -4.7% | 0.75 | WC drag persists, fixed-price overruns, margin stays at the FY2024 trough | $72.08 | 5.53% |
| Bear | 30% | 2.3% | 0.90 | Revenue grows on backlog but cash conversion stays FY2024-like | $118.06 | 7.96% |
| Base | 30% | 7.3% | 1.00 | Backlog converts at recent margins; OE lumpiness averages out at the median base | $163.88 | 10.28% |
| Bull | 15% | 12.3% | 1.10 | Throughput and margin recovery toward the raised guidance range and beyond | $225.08 | 13.11% |
| Super bull | 10% | 19.3% | 1.25 | Submarine/carrier supercycle plus a return to pre-2021 margins | $348.39 | 17.96% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $163.99 (−39.3% vs price), IV@12% $220.00, IV@10% $282.76, IV@20% $114.06, IV@25% $86.84; weighted IRR 10.33%, base-case IRR 10.28%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Bear tier D (7.96%), bull tier C (13.11%). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 5.98%, terminal value 19.8% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.83x, net debt 3.04x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 10 months ago): resolved by running ttm.py — its legs are quoted above. The TTM base (−$3.48/share) was *rejected* with a written reason: it is a working-capital timing trough (H1 2026 OCF −$421M against reiterated $500–$600M full-year FCF guidance), the same artifact that makes single-year OE unusable at this company. The normalized median base is retained; the TTM information is instead carried into the scenario weights.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real and structural — FY2024 $0.08 to FY2025 $18.83 is contract/WC timing, not a one-off error. Handled by (a) the 3-year median base and (b) widening the bear weight: probabilities 15/30/30/15/10 put 45% on bear-or-worse vs 35% by default.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025 NI vs OCF differ by >40%): FY2025 net income $605M vs OCF $1,196M. From the 10-K cash-flow table found in research: D&A $329M, SBC $54M, deferred income taxes +$203M (a $325M swing from −$122M in FY2024), retiree benefits −$154M, trade working capital a $170M *decrease* (a $430M swing from a $260M increase in FY2024), gain on marketable securities −$34M. The divergence is noncash addbacks plus the deferred-tax and working-capital swings — no impairment or tax-deposit one-off. Implication for the base: FY2025 OCF (and its $18.83 OE/share) is flattered by those swings, which is exactly why the median ($16.14), not the latest year, is the base.
- **CASH_INCLUDES_RESTRICTED**: fundamentals.json confirms the latest cash basis is the combined `CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents` tag ($774,000,000) with no separate restricted-cash tag, so reported net debt of $1,926,000,000 is understated by whatever restricted amount is inside that $774M. No figure for the restricted portion is in the computed outputs, so it is stated in words only: true net debt is higher than $1.926B, which strengthens, not weakens, the HIGH_NET_DEBT caution below. The verdict does not rest on the precise net-debt figure.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.83x super-bear IV): real — the outcome range at a shipbuilder whose OE can print $0.08 or $18.83 in adjacent years IS wide. Confidence is capped at low (below), and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 3.04x normalized OE): balance sheet from the filing data in financials_history.csv latest row: cash $774,000,000 (combined incl. restricted, above), long-term debt $2,700,000,000, net debt $1,926,000,000, plus operating lease liabilities $281,000,000 not in the net-debt figure. At 3.04x normalized OE (dcf_numbers.json diagnostics), leverage is material for a business whose OE can near-vanish in a bad WC year (FY2024). Interim update from statements.json (2026-06-30): total debt $2,702,000,000 against cash of $12,000,000 — net debt of ≈$2,690,000,000, ≈4.2x normalized OE and $764M above the FY-end figure. That is the same H1 working-capital trough behind the negative TTM (filed quarterly cash prints in statements.json range from $10,000,000 to $1,057,000,000, so a point-in-time interim balance overstates the structural position), but on the latest filed balance sheet leverage is higher than the FY-end diagnostic shows, which reinforces rather than changes this resolution. Reflected in the 45% bear-or-worse weight; no separate tier adjustment, because the bear scenarios already stress OE directly.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D 7.96% vs bull tier C 13.11%): sized to the bear end in the sizing sense, and the tier itself is deliberately not overridden down to D, for a stated reason: the weighted IRR of 10.33% already embeds a deliberately widened 45% bear-or-worse probability mass (15/30 on super bear/bear vs 35% by default, per the OE_VOLATILE resolution), so the band is a property of the weighted result rather than an unscored upside case; the hurdle price quoted throughout is the weighted IV@15 of $163.99, not the bull IV of $225.08; and anyone sizing a position off this page should plan on the bear case — IV@15 $118.06 at a 7.96% IRR, i.e. Tier D economics. The defensible range is D–C; the published tier is the weighted C.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the range: even the super-bull case (19.3% OE growth start, 1.25x OE) only reaches a 17.96% IRR at $270 — no scenario in the set clears 20%. The stock at $270 prices in a margin/throughput recovery that the last five years of ROIC (6.5–10.2%) and operating margin (4.6–6.8%) do not yet show.
- Quality is not the debate: the franchise position is as durable as any in U.S. defense, backlog is $57.3B and growing, revenue is compounding at 5–11%, and SBC is trivial ($54M FY2025).
